answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can use bonded identity deposits. Each new agent posts a collateral bond that burns on consensus detection of fake behavior. An attacker must lock fresh capital for every identity they create, raising costs linearly as they wander beyond a single plume of activity toward the economic horizon where the cumulative bond burden exceeds any short-term gain from multiplicity. Established agents face lower ongoing requirements, concentrating risk on newcomers.
